name: Black Red
lede: Black Red is a very dark red, so dark that it is close to black, listed as RAL 3007 in the German paint standard.

sections.title: A descriptive name
sections.body:
Black Red is a plain description, a red darkened until it nearly reads as black [1]. In our library it is the paint-chart color RAL 3007, and the screen value is approximate [1]. The earliest record of the name in our sources is 1927 [1]. Its nearest widely used name is [[oxblood]], about 12 units away on the CIEDE2000 scale [1].

Our library also pairs the swatch with the Japanese traditional name *nisemurasaki*, "fake purple" [1]. No book in our collection explains that pairing, so treat it as a library entry only [1].

sections.title: The pair, not the color
sections.body:
Books that mention [[black]] and [[red]] together are almost always talking about two colors side by side. Pastoureau tells how chess began with black and red pieces in India and in Islamic lands, a pair of opposites in Asia from time immemorial [2]. When the game reached Europe around the year 1000, the opposition changed to white against red, and from the mid-thirteenth century to the white against black we know now [2].

In Gothic art, black and red together stood for the devil: black body, red flames of hell and the blood of the damned, as in Fra Angelico's *Last Judgment* of about 1431 to 1432 [3]. Medieval discriminatory marks drew on five colors, and red and black were among the most frequent combinations [4]. None of these is the single dark red of the swatch.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color near this swatch appears in 525 works, or 2.21 per cent, which makes it more common than 80 per cent of the named colors [5]. It peaks in the 1500s, in 59 of 2,231 paintings, 1.5 times the museums' baseline [5]. Inside a painting it is most often a hidden color, in 59 per cent of the 384 works where we measure it by lightness rank [5].

It travels with [[brown-red]] and [[black-blue]] on the same canvases, at 9.0 and 4.2 times chance [5]. The earliest match is dated 1270, long before the name existed, so it is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a record of the paint [5]. The Google Books curve for the words also peaks in the 1870s, but it counts every use of the two words and says little about the color [6].

questions.q: In the original Indian and Islamic chess, which two colors faced each other?
When chess spread to Europe around the year 1000, what did the opposition become?

openers: Chess pieces were black and red in India; Europe made them white and red, then white and black.

issues: No book treats Black Red as a single color; mentions are of the pair.
